title: Continuous batch warmup playbook - scratch
content:
Goal: quick scratchpad to capture commands tried, ephemeral hypotheses, and a repeatable checklist for reproducing a throughput drop tied to continuous batching + KV cache warmup. Save here before I turn this into a proper runbook.

Incident summary (short):
- Observed throughput drop (~25-40% p95 throughput) on model rwd/opt-14b-qat when new routing started sending 2x requests with short prefixes (avg 8 tokens). Spike correlates with instance recycle and CPU-bound kernel selection during first 300ms of each new connection.
- Pattern: cold workers (newly scaled nodes) service a flurry of short-prefix requests; continuous-batcher appears to open tiny micro-batches that don't trigger KV cache warmup; runtime falls back to slower attention kernel for first N steps.

Why I think it's warmup related:
- Telemetry: token-level cost/latency breakdown shows high "compile/kernel-select" and "kv-populate" spikes on worker boot up
- Flamegraphs from perf show heavy memcpy + small-matrix-gemm paths for first 150 tokens served by a node
- When I pin requests to already-warmed nodes, throughput returns to baseline

Quick timeline:
- 2025-01-16 09:12 UTC: Canary rollout of routing policy A->B begins (traffic shift ~15%)
- 2025-01-16 09:20 UTC: Autoscaler creates 6 new pods to handle burst
- 2025-01-16 09:21-09:40 UTC: Throughput drops on user-facing route; error rates unchanged, latency slightly higher
- 2025-01-16 10:05 UTC: Manual traffic pin to older pool confirmed throughput recovery

Commands & experiments I ran (raw):
- kubectl logs -n serving runtime-pool-5f9d -c runtime | grep -i "kv" -A3 -B1
  -> snippets show repeated "kv cache miss prefetcher: initial miss, scheduling warmup" messages

- rwd-admin exec --node runtime-pool-5f9d -- /bin/bash -c "ps aux | grep runtime_worker" && /usr/local/bin/trace_vma --pid $(pgrep runtime_worker) --output /tmp/trace.pf
  -> traced early allocations, saw many small allocations then a large contiguous allocation (~1.2GB) after first completed request

- perf record -F 99 -p $(pgrep runtime_worker) --call-graph=dwarf -o /tmp/perf.data  (during warmup)
  perf script | flamegraph.pl > /tmp/fg-warmup.svg
  -> hot path points to attention_kernel_generic + kv_prefetch path

- toggled runtime flags in the config map to test effect (rolled config with restart):
  continuous_batcher.enabled: false
  batch_window_ms: 25 -> 10
  max_batch_tokens: 2048 -> 4096
  kv_prefetch.concurrent_limit: 8 -> 2
  -> immediate effect: disabling continuous-batcher recovered throughput but increased p99 latency on long requests. Lowering batch_window reduced the number of micro-batches but didn't fully recover.

- A/B test: route 50% traffic to variant with continuous_batcher.prefetch_threshold=6
  Observed: when threshold > average prefix length, throughput stabilizes for that subset.

Representative log + error snippets:
- [2025-01-16T09:21:02Z] INFO runtime: starting request id=abc-123 prefix_len=7
- [2025-01-16T09:21:02Z] DEBUG batcher: created micro-batch size=2 wait_ms=12
- [2025-01-16T09:21:02Z] WARN kv: cache miss for shard=34 key=KV-xyz scheduling warmup
- [2025-01-16T09:21:02Z] INFO kernel-select: chosen=attention_generic reason=kv_not_cached
- [2025-01-16T09:21:02Z] INFO kernel-select: fallback to quant-attn-slow (no optimized GEMM found)
- [2025-01-16T09:21:03Z] DEBUG perf: compile-time-ms=118

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Continuous-batcher is creating many tiny micro-batches on cold nodes which trigger slow attention kernels and force non-optimized code paths because KV cache wasn't populated. The overhead dominates short-prefix workloads.
2) KV prefetcher concurrency/ordering interacts poorly with autoscaler: when many nodes start in parallel, prefetch flood saturates memcpy/PCIe and causes kernel selection to fallback to safer generic kernels.
3) Batch window tuning + max_batch_tokens mismatch means micro-batches are too frequent and never reach the size threshold that would allow kernel autotuning to pick fast kernels.
4) CUDA kernel cache warming (jit/cubin) occurs lazily on first use; our runtime may be serializing compile + prefetch and starving request threads.
5) Scheduling quirk: the worker thread that handles batch dispatch is also doing large KV population work synchronously, blocking subsequent batches.

Minimal repro steps to run locally (devbox):
- Start 3 local runtime instances with latest image and set continuous_batcher.enabled=true and kv_prefetch.concurrent_limit=8
- Use load-test script (simple python): send requests with payloads of 6-9 token prefixes at QPS 120 for 10m targeting new instances only (use header x-target-node)
- Capture /metrics and /debug/trace endpoints, and record perf on one instance for first 90s

Quick mitigation options (fast):
- Pin critical customer routes to warmed pools (traffic steering) until we have a proper fix
- Temporarily disable continuous-batcher for routes with short-prefix traffic
- Reduce kv_prefetch.concurrent_limit to prevent PCIe saturation during scale-up
- Add a pre-warm job: after node creation, run a small synthetic request sequence to populate KV and compile kernels (cheap warmup)

Longer-term fixes to test:
- Make kernel selection prefer warm fast kernel by checking a separate warm flag (avoid fallback on first few requests)
- Make KV prefetch asynchronous and rate-limited per-NUMA to avoid cross-node saturation
- Change continuous-batcher heuristics: require minimum prefix length or minimum aggregated token count before dispatching micro-batch to allow kernel autotuning
- Add an early warmup step in autoscaler: run warmup template on new instances and consider readiness only when warmup complete

What I need next (todo):
- [ ] Turn repro into a CI scenario (GH:serving-runtime#4821) and add perf capture hooks
- [ ] Confirm whether quantized kernels also exhibit same behavior (run on uint8/4-bit variant)
- [ ] Check kernel cache metrics: how many JIT compilations happened during the incident (collect from /debug/kernel-cache)
- [ ] Ask infra to expose PCIe memcpy counters on the node pool during next scale test
- [ ] Draft a minimal playbook for SRE-run mitigation (traffic pin, disable cbatcher)

Notes to self / random observations:
- When I manually replayed the exact request pattern on a single warm node, throughput was fine; suggests node-local state is critical
- Lowering batch_window_ms too far increases overhead (context switches) — there's a sweet spot
- The prefetch log message ordering sometimes shows "scheduling warmup" after the kernel-select, which implies we try kernels before KV attempt completes -> race

Links for context:
- GH: redwood-inference/serving-runtime#4821 (PR with cbatcher telemetry) 
- JIRA: INF-2279 (incident)
- Slack: #serving-runtime Jan 17 thread (contains perf svgs)

If I don't get back to this in 48h: pin route, disable cbatcher for that route, and hand to SRE for on-call mitigation. Save traces to artifacts/INF-2279/warmup/.

End of scratchpad.
